label: What the viewer shows
description: Which kinds of files Dayspring's file viewer shows on the screen, and how. Everything is read on this computer (nothing is uploaded); files are only opened from folders allowed in Settings → Permissions. "Passes simulator tests" means the automated tests open a made-up file of that kind in headless Chrome and use its controls (scripts/qa/file-viewer.mjs).

entries.notes: The EXIF date taken, camera and size are read from the file itself; the GPS location is never shown or sent anywhere.
howToSetUp: Allow the folder in Settings → Permissions with "Can look".
Say "show me the picture named …".

entries.notes: Shown by the screen's browser itself. AVIF works in current Chrome and Edge.
howToSetUp: Allow the folder in Settings → Permissions.

entries.notes: Shown as a picture only, in a sandbox: any script inside it never runs.
howToSetUp: Allow the folder in Settings → Permissions.

capabilities: shown as a JPEG decoded by Windows
entries.notes: Decoded by Windows' own HEIF decoder through Dayspring's picture helper. The tests use a HEIF file with an AV1 picture (ffmpeg can't write HEVC ones); iPhone photos (HEVC) also need Microsoft's HEVC Video Extensions. Without the decoder, "Open in the default app" still works.
howToSetUp: Install "HEIF Image Extensions" (free) and "HEVC Video Extensions" from the Microsoft Store if HEIC photos don't show.
Allow the folder in Settings → Permissions.

capabilities: shown as a JPEG decoded by Windows
entries.notes: Decoded by Windows (the same path as HEIC); the first page only.
howToSetUp: Allow the folder in Settings → Permissions.

entries.notes: Streamed with HTTP Range, so seeking is instant. MP4 with H.264 is tested; WebM and MOV play when the screen's browser has the codec.
howToSetUp: Allow the folder in Settings → Permissions.
Put captions next to the video with the same name: movie.mp4 and movie.srt (or movie.en.srt).

capabilities: converted to MP4 as it plays
entries.notes: Converted on the fly by Dayspring's ffmpeg (ffmpeg-static), like the media library. WMV is tested.
howToSetUp: Nothing to set up; if ffmpeg isn't there, use "Open in the default app".

entries.model: MP3, M4A, AAC, FLAC, WAV, OGG, Opus (WMA converted)
entries.notes: MP3 is tested; the others play in Chrome and Edge. WMA is converted by ffmpeg.
howToSetUp: Allow the folder in Settings → Permissions.

entries.notes: Drawn by pdf.js (Mozilla, Apache-2.0), shipped with Dayspring in public/vendor/pdfjs. PDFs with a password open only in the default app. Scanned PDFs (no text) show fine, but search and read aloud need text.
howToSetUp: Allow the folder in Settings → Permissions.

entries.model: Text and code (TXT, LOG, JSON, JS, TS, PY, CS, CSS, HTML, XML, YAML, SQL, PS1, BAT and more)
entries.notes: Highlighting by Prism (MIT), shipped in public/vendor/prism. The first 2 MB is shown. HTML and XML are shown as text, never run.
howToSetUp: Allow the folder in Settings → Permissions.

entries.notes: Formatted by the viewer itself: everything is escaped first, so HTML or scripts inside never run, and pictures from the internet aren't loaded.
howToSetUp: Allow the folder in Settings → Permissions.

capabilities: sort by a column (numbers as numbers)
entries.notes: Read by SheetJS Community Edition 0.20.3 (Apache-2.0), installed from cdn.sheetjs.com: the "xlsx" package on the npm registry is an older 0.18.5 with known problems, so Dayspring doesn't use it. The first 2,000 rows and 60 columns are shown; formulas show their values.
howToSetUp: Allow the folder in Settings → Permissions.

capabilities: headings, lists, tables, bold and italic
entries.notes: Turned into a clean page by mammoth (BSD-2-Clause) and cleaned again (sanitize-html): no scripts, no pictures from the internet. Page layout (columns, headers, exact fonts) isn't reproduced.
howToSetUp: Allow the folder in Settings → Permissions.

capabilities: the text, in paragraphs and headings
entries.notes: Shown as text through Dayspring's document reader (lib/documents.mjs); .doc files may need Word installed.
howToSetUp: Allow the folder in Settings → Permissions.

entries.notes: The slides' words and pictures, not their design or animations. For the real look, open it in PowerPoint ("Open in the default app").
howToSetUp: Allow the folder in Settings → Permissions.

entries.reason: There's no pure-JavaScript reader for these formats that could be shipped with Dayspring. The viewer shows the file's details and opens it in its usual app.

capabilities: open a small file inside (up to 25 MB)
entries.notes: Read by JSZip. Files inside that look secret or private are never opened; a file that grows past the limit while unpacking is stopped.
howToSetUp: Allow the folder in Settings → Permissions.

entries.reason: No pure-JavaScript reader for them is shipped (they'd need a native program). The viewer shows the file's details and opens it in its usual app.

capabilities: info card (name, type, size, dates, folder)
open in the default app (Programs permission)
entries.notes: Opening another program needs the Programs permission and asks first when it's set to ask; a file that runs when opened always asks.
howToSetUp: Allow Programs in Settings → Permissions to open files in their usual apps.
